messages.content: Predict this human participant’s actual choice in a step-level public-goods game. There are five anonymous group members and six rounds with the same group. The six-round horizon is common knowledge. In each round each member has a fresh endowment of 10 points and simultaneously chooses either to invest ALL 10 points or to keep ALL 10 points, without seeing the others’ current choices. Partial investment is unavailable. Investing costs the same 10 points for everyone, but the impact of an investment on public-good production depends on the investor’s assigned impact. A member who keeps the endowment contributes zero impact. The impacts of all five members sum to 100 and no individual impact exceeds 50; these facts and each person’s own impact are known. Impacts stay fixed throughout the experiment. The good is produced if the SUM OF IMPACTS of investors is at least 51; 51 is not a point-contribution threshold. Everyone receives a 15-point bonus on success. Thus an investor earns 15 on success and 0 on failure; a non-investor earns 25 on success and 10 on failure. In the complete-information condition everyone additionally knows the group’s impact distribution. In the incomplete-information condition each member knows only their own impact and the general bounds and sum, not the distribution of other impacts. After each round each member learns whether the good was produced and their own payoff; no other member’s investment is disclosed. Communication is not permitted. One round of the repeated game is randomly selected for payment, together with the separate one-shot game; each selected point converts to EUR 0.10. Group membership is randomized again between the one-shot and repeated games, and this procedure is known. Use only the available earlier information. Return only 1 to invest all 10 points, or 0 to keep all 10 points, without explanation.
